purpose: Cyclophosphamide is used to treat certain types of cancer, such as lymphoma, leukemia, breast cancer, and others. It is also sometimes used to calm down an overactive immune system in conditions like lupus or certain kidney diseases. Your doctor has chosen this medicine because it can help slow down or stop the growth of harmful cells in your body.
how_it_works: This medicine works by getting into the DNA of fast-growing cells and interfering with their ability to copy themselves and grow. Think of it like putting a wrench in the machinery that cancer cells — or overactive immune cells — use to multiply. Because of this, those harmful cells slow down, stop growing, or die off.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting, hair loss (usually temporary), mouth sores, loss of appetite, low blood counts (which can increase your risk of infection, bruising, or tiredness), and bladder irritation or blood in the urine. Drinking plenty of water helps protect your bladder.
warnings: This medicine can seriously lower your immune system, making it easier to catch infections — contact your doctor right away if you have a fever. It can cause bladder bleeding, so drink lots of fluids and tell your doctor if you see blood in your urine. It may affect fertility in both men and women, so talk to your doctor before starting if this is a concern. Avoid contact with people who are sick, and do not get live vaccines while on this medication.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on why you are taking it, your weight or body size, and your kidney function. It can be given as a pill by mouth or as an intravenous (IV) infusion in a clinic. Your doctor or cancer care team will set the exact schedule — it may be daily, weekly, or in cycles. Always follow the schedule your care team gives you.
